research_context.original_topic: How can we measure interface phenomena on the microscopic level? Interfacial chemistry seeks to deepen our understanding of molecular interfaces between gases and liquids, liquids and solids, and solids and solids. At microscopic and nanoscale boundaries, mass and heat transfer occur through evaporation, reactions, and micro- or nanoscale explosive events, yet the chemical mechanisms that choreograph these processes remain incompletely understood. Optical interference methods can measure gas-film or liquid-film thickness at gas-liquid and liquid-solid interfaces down to the nanoscale, but this information is insufficient to resolve complex interfacial physical and chemical phenomena. Improved microscopic-interface measurement is urgently needed for materials synthesis, combustion, spray drying, and next-generation evaporative-cooling nanodevices.
